method: Independent complete-source bilingual review against docs/ANNOTATION_RUBRIC.md, before inference. Candidate IDs generated mechanically by action_decomposition.propose_spans. Gate positives require a concrete recipient operation or repeated explicit task obligation; shared imperative verbs count, bare field/object fragments do not. Navigation and repeated directives belong to the same task; explicit invitations including optional opt-outs count. Task groups may overlap when one candidate repeats multiple operations. All 40 paired labels and task lists agree; no text/label corrections recommended.

issues.issue: An explicit obligation repeats both operations in one candidate, so candidate task groups overlap. Do not assume a partition of candidates.
One broad repeated imperative covers two operations; candidate groups overlap, but this does not create a third task.
One broad repeated imperative covers two operations; candidate groups overlap, but this does not create a third task.

Some coordinated candidates are bare fields or objects and have no operation, while others inherit a shared imperative verb. Gate annotations distinguish these by full-message meaning. A task operation can be recoverable from context despite an incomplete isolated span.
Alternatives share a task group, but their pair relationship is alternatives rather than same_task_steps; explicit pair annotations are retained.

Development and heldout were balanced by boundary types but several messages remain close structural paraphrases with changed topics. They should be grouped before final split; current holdout supports topic transfer on familiar constructions, not unseen template transfer. All provisional heldout rows below have a close development structural analogue; do not claim a template-disjoint split.
